newsitem.title: USA: Profits of big U.S. retailers rose in second quarter.
newsitem.headline: Profits of big U.S. retailers rose in second quarter.

text.p: Profits of big U.S. retailers climbed strongly in the second quarter, to $3.87 billion from $2.84 billion in the first three months of the year, the Commerce Department said Wednesday.
Total sales were up to $233.25 billion from $225.34 billion in the first quarter.
As a result, companies' earnings per sales dollar, after paying taxes, increased to 1.7 cents in the second quarter from a revised 1.3 cents in the first quarter.
Previously, the department said first-quarter profits were 1.2 cents on each dollar of sales.

The national economy expanded briskly at a 4.7 percent annual rate during the second quarter, the strongest advance in quarterly gross domestic product in two years, the Commerce Department previously reported. Growth is expected to slow to around half that rate in the final six months of the year.
In the second quarter of 1995, retailers' profits were $3.62 billion, or 1.7 cents per sales dollar, and total sales were $218.44 billion.
This year's second-quarter findings were based on quarterly financial reports obtained from 546 large retail corporations. They were not adjusted for seasonal variation.
All the companies had assets of $50 million or more.
